title: Positive derived inverse limits of explicit finite-prefix towers vanish
statement: Let $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Ab})$ be the abelian category of towers [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-pc-tower-abelian], assume it has enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives], and assume $L=\varprojlim:\mathcal T\to\mathrm{Ab}$ is additive, so its right derived functors $R^q L$ are defined [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For every tower $A$, every $s\in\mathbf N$, and every $q\ge1$, $R^qL(T_s(A))=0$, where $T_s(A)_n=\prod_{i<n+s}A_i$ with restriction transitions [lem-pc-roos-finite-prefix-construction].

proof.text: Prove all composite transitions of a tower with surjective successor transitions surjective by induction on the target index. Mathlib Functor.isMittagLeffler_of_surjective then proves its underlying-set tower is Mittag--Leffler. Apply this to the finite-prefix tower using roosPrefix_transition_surjective (extension by zero, including the empty prefix).

For each Mittag--Leffler tower B, obtain a monomorphism i:B→I from tower_injective_embedding. The levels of I are injective and its successor transitions split. The theorem injective_of_injective_split_tower makes I injective as a tower. Construct Q as cokernel i and use Mathlib cokernelSequence_exact and Mono i for the short exact sequence S:0→B→I→Q→0. Exactness of evaluation gives termwise short exactness.

Use the existing horseshoe right-derived delta-functor for lim. For degree one, mittagLeffler_quotient_and_limit_exact (3) makes lim.map S.g epic since B is ML. Mathlib rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf transfers this to R⁰lim.map S.g. Exactness to its right makes the connecting map zero. Exactness at R¹lim B, with R¹lim I=0 by Mathlib isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ, therefore makes R¹lim B zero.

Induct on the positive degree simultaneously for every ML tower B. The split successor transitions of I are surjective, so the first step proves I is ML. By mittagLeffler_quotient_and_limit_exact (2), Q is ML. At degree q+2, exactness of R^(q+1)lim Q→R^(q+2)lim B→R^(q+2)lim I makes the middle term zero: the left term vanishes by induction and the right term by injectivity of I. Apply this induction to the explicit finite-prefix tower.
